topic_candidates.title: Almost literally EVERYONE is wrong about foldable phones
topic_candidates.query: Apple iPhone Duo foldable durability hinge crease display review 2026
topic_candidates.brief: Instead of asking whether Apple made the perfect foldable, the video explains why people are judging the iPhone Duo by the wrong standard. Folding phones are a compromise between two rigid slabs and one flexible display: the hinge, crease, dust protection, thickness, cameras and software all compete for the same limited space. Viewers see why a device can feel revolutionary and still have problems that ordinary phones solved years ago.
topic_candidates.evidence_summary: Apple confirms that iPhone Duo is its first foldable iPhone. Independent testing reported more than 32,000 folds in one test, while other coverage documented display-cracking complaints affecting some units. The narrative should distinguish controlled testing, individual reports and confirmed product specifications rather than claiming that every Duo fails.

topic_candidates.science_angle: Flexible OLED fatigue, hinge mechanics, crease stress, particle ingress, repeated-cycle testing and the physics of bending a multilayer display.

topic_candidates.title: OpenAI spent $1.2 million securing Linux... and it was a bargain
topic_candidates.query: OpenAI 948 Linux privilege escalation exploits 1.2 million official research
topic_candidates.brief: An AI system was used to inspect Linux code, reproduce suspected bugs, test whether they could become real attacks, generate exploits and propose patches. The important point for normal people is that this was not a robot remotely taking over 948 random computers: the headline number refers to local privilege-escalation bugs, where a program that already has limited access can potentially gain root-level control. The video explains why automated bug discovery could make both defense and offense faster.
topic_candidates.evidence_summary: OpenAI says its pipeline reproduced 1,724 vulnerabilities and produced 948 working local privilege-escalation exploits in a mid-October 2026 run costing $1,213,430 in API credits. The company describes candidate patches and human review as part of the process, so the story should not claim that all 948 flaws were immediately deployed or that every Linux machine was exposed remotely.
topic_candidates.broke_on: OpenAI spent $1.2 million hacking Linux... and it was a bargain — Fireship, breakout 0.7, source breakout 3
topic_candidates.science_angle: Automated vulnerability discovery, privilege boundaries, exploit chains, sandboxing, reproducibility and the economics of defensive cybersecurity.

topic_candidates.title: Fable 5.2 is different
topic_candidates.query: Anthropic Claude Fable 5.2 launch capabilities speed price safety system card
topic_candidates.brief: The video cuts through the benchmark excitement around Anthropic’s new frontier model and asks what changes for a normal person. Fable 5.2 is presented as a system that can handle longer, more complicated technical tasks, but the useful explanation is about delegation: the model can plan, use tools and keep working through multiple stages, while users still need to check its assumptions and results. The story also examines why stronger capability and stronger safeguards are being released together.
topic_candidates.evidence_summary: Anthropic announced Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 on November 9, 2026. The company reports improvements in coding, reasoning and vision, output up to 30% faster than version 5.1, lower listed pricing, and separate safeguards and availability for Fable and Mythos. These are company-reported capabilities, so the video should label performance examples as Anthropic’s claims rather than independent proof of general intelligence.

topic_candidates.title: Starship - Go For Catch
topic_candidates.query: SpaceX Starship Flight 15 booster catch Starlink V3 November 2026 official
topic_candidates.brief: The next Starship test is not just about reaching orbit. The engineering challenge is recovering a booster that has burned through most of its fuel, re-entered at high speed and must line up with mechanical catching arms at the launch tower. The video explains why catching the booster could make a large rocket reusable quickly, while also showing how the mission’s Starlink payload gives SpaceX a practical reason to fly it.
topic_candidates.evidence_summary: SpaceX says Starship is designed as a fully reusable system and that future flights will deploy next-generation Starlink satellites. Public mission coverage identifies a planned opportunity for a booster catch and Starlink V3 deployment, but the video should describe the catch as an objective or opportunity, not a guaranteed success before the flight occurs.
